content: William Goldberg is a social worker and researcher specializing in the study of cults. He operates a private practice where he provides counseling to families of individuals involved in cults. Additionally, he is employed by the Rockland County Department of Mental Health in New York, where he oversees three outpatient mental health programs. Goldberg has been invited to testify before various state legislatures on topics related to the regulation of adult home residents and cult-related issues. Specifically, he has provided testimony to the New York State Assembly Committee on Child Care, the New York State Social Service Committee, the New Jersey State Assembly Judiciary Committee, and the Connecticut State Judiciary Committee. As an expert commentator, Mr. Goldberg has appeared on prominent media platforms, including ABC News, The Sally Jesse Raphael Show, The John McLaughlin Show, MSNBC, and The Geraldo Rivera Show. Alongside his wife, Lorna Goldberg, he has co-led a support group for former cult members for over 25 years. In recognition of their work, Bill and Lorna Goldberg were awarded the Leo J. Ryan Award by the Leo J. Ryan Education Foundation in 1999. The Goldbergs co-authored an article titled Group Work with Former Cultists, which was published in the journal Social Work. William Goldberg has also contributed to numerous other publications and reports, including works prepared for Boston University’s Danielsen Institute and articles in journals such as the Cultic Studies Journal. His writings include topics like family responses to cult membership, counseling cult-impacted students, and mental health approaches to recovery from abusive groups. He has been recognized with awards such as the Hall of Fame Award from the Cult Awareness Network. His contributions to the field include a preface to Wendy Ford’s Recovery from Abusive Groups and chapters in books like The Boston Movement, edited by Carol Giambalvo and Herbert L. Rosedale. Additionally, he has written on topics such as Cold Reading: The Tricks of the Psychics and has contributed to newsletters and journals aimed at supporting former cult members.
